newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end listless trade slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares end listless trade slightly higher.

text.p: Electronic trade in German shares ended on Wednesday with the IBIS DAX index in positive territory, matching the bourse closing level from earlier on in trade mostly driven by derivatives.
Share trade over the day was directionless and lacklustre, with shares were unable to either forge new gains or deliver the correction some traders were seeking.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade, ended at 3,730.56 points, up 9.38 points or 0.25 percent. Earlier the DAX index, which tracks bourse trade, ended at 3,730.27 points, down 11.21 points or 0.30 percent, while the June DAX future ended at 3,726.5 points, up 7.5.
Dealers said the influence of a weaker close on Wall Street overnight and the lower dollar against the mark was hard to shake off.
The futures contract was higher ahead of Friday's triple-witching expiry, where DAX futures, DAX options and stock options expire, was also leading to some nervousness in the market.
Traders said that derivative-led business was not representative of fundamentals in the market.
Wall Street's close overnight, down 0.15 percent at 7,760.78 points, as well as a lower opening, was insufficient to deliver the correction that many share traders have been seeking of late.
The DAX has been trading in or around record levels in recent days, and many market players reckon that it is overpriced at this level.
However, as long as Wall Street's rise kept continuing, the harder it was not to be in the market. With breathing space now on the horizon, dealers were hoping for a healthy consolidation.
Also impacting on trading sentiment was the softer dollar. Again this proved not enough to bring about any kind of correction, but it did impact on dollar-led stocks.
